tip: 'Caso' meaning if or in case forces the subjunctive: 'ligue', not 'liga'.
Here 'nos' means each other, not ourselves: 'nos abraçamos' is we hugged one another.
'Acostumar-se' pairs with 'com' to mark what you get used to: 'se acostumaram com o calor', got used to the heat.
'Para' with a time marks a deadline, meaning by: 'para amanhã' is by tomorrow, not for tomorrow.
When the person you describe doesn't exist, the verb goes subjunctive: 'ninguém que saiba', no one who knows.
In a question it stays two words, 'por que'; the one-word 'porque' means because and belongs in the answer.
'Embora' (although) always takes the subjunctive: 'embora a comida esteja fria', not 'está fria'.
Imperfeito 'chovia' sets the ongoing background, while preterite 'chegou' marks the single event that cut in.
'Querer que' always triggers the subjunctive whenever one person wants another to do something: 'quero que ninguém saiba', not 'sabe'.
'Para mim' = for me (opinion/benefit). Don't confuse with 'por mim' = as far as I'm concerned / on my behalf.
'Tinha' plus a participle is the pluperfect, an action done before another past event: 'tinha começado', had started.
'Há' plus a time span means ago: 'há dois anos' is two years ago. Note the spelling 'há', not 'a'.
Two simultaneous ongoing actions both use imperfeito: 'falava' and 'anotava' were happening at the same time.
'Obrigado por' = thank you for. Use 'por' when thanking someone for something they already did. It's about the reason for your gratitude.
'Demitir-se' means to quit your own job. Drop the 'se' and 'demitir' means to fire someone. 'Ela se demitiu' = she resigned.
In casual Brazilian Portuguese the command uses the 'ele' form: 'fala', not the textbook 'fale'. 'Fala mais devagar' = speak more slowly.
'Fazer a barba' literally means to make the beard, but it is the normal way to say to shave. 'Eu me cortei fazendo a barba' = I cut myself shaving.
'Dar-se conta de' is a set phrase for to realize or become aware. 'Nós nos demos conta do erro' = we realized the mistake.
'A gente' means we in casual speech but takes a singular verb like 'ele'. That is why it is 'se comunica', not 'comunicam'.
'Por' here means on behalf of or in defense of: 'lutou por seus direitos' = she fought for her rights.
'Foi preso' is passive: 'ser' plus a past participle. 'Preso' agrees with the subject, so a woman would be 'foi presa'.
The 'o' before 'conheço' means him, a direct object pronoun sitting in front of the verb. In speech many say 'não conheço ele' instead.
'Lembrar-se de' means 'to remember.' The 'se' makes it reflexive. You can also say 'lembrar de' without 'se' – both are correct in Brazil.
'Apaixonar-se' takes 'por' for what you fall for, and 'por' plus 'o' contracts to 'pelo'. 'Eu me apaixonei pelo Brasil' = I fell in love with Brazil.
'Para' for deadlines: 'para quando' = by when, 'para amanhã' = by tomorrow, 'para sexta' = by Friday.
'Há' plus a length of time means ago: 'há cinco anos' = five years ago. It comes from 'haver', not from 'ter'.
'Para' plus an infinitive states purpose, the why: 'para ajudar' means in order to help.
'Divertir-se' is reflexive in Portuguese: 'você se diverte' = you have fun. 'Vocês se divertiram na festa' = did you have fun at the party.
'Conhecer' usually means to know, but with 'nos' (each other) it means to meet for the first time. 'Nós nos conhecemos numa festa' = we met at a party.
'Gostar' normally needs 'de' before its object, but when the thing is already clear you can drop it: 'não gostei' = I didn't like it.
